item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 42, 2026
item.description:
This week the theme is scale: what breaks when agents write, merge and review code faster than any human can keep up. Five posts cover Anthropic’s new dynamic workflows for Claude Managed Agents, the in-house version control system built to replace git, OpenTelemetry traces for agents, a paper on recursive self-improvement through multi-agent self-supervision, and how the Claude Code team reviews code at agent volume.

If last week was about letting go of the steering wheel safely, this week is about the road, the bridges and the traffic cameras that need rebuilding once everyone is driving at 30,000 merges a day. Grab a coffee, and let’s dive in.

item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 41, 2026
item.description:
This week the theme is small, sharp and scheduled: tiny models that decide, harnesses that learn, and agents that quietly do their job while you sleep. Six posts cover System 1 “decider” models with a working router, Microsoft’s lightweight agentic RL framework, Claude Code mods, Pinterest’s LLM-powered user journeys, an AI-assisted learning framework, and Anthropic’s recipe for agent automations that don’t fail silently.

If last week was about who holds the steering wheel, this week is about what happens when you let go of it, safely. Grab a coffee, and let’s dive in.

item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 24, 2026
item.description:
What a week to be paying attention. We swing from a Claude Code creator who merges 150 PRs a day from his phone, through the quiet plumbing of agents that run on a schedule, to the launch of the most capable model Anthropic has ever shipped, and then to that same model being yanked off the shelves by a government directive 72 hours later.

If you ever needed proof that the AI story in 2026 is as much about governance and infrastructure as it is about raw capability, this is the week. Grab a coffee; there’s a lot to unpack, and I’ve got opinions on most of it.

item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 21, 2026
item.description:
This week’s roundup is dominated by a single seismic event: Andrej Karpathy has joined Anthropic. The most beloved AI teacher in the world, a founding member of OpenAI, and former lead of Tesla Autopilot, is now working on using Claude to improve Claude. Meanwhile, Anthropic quietly shipped something that changes the economics of agent development entirely: Claude Managed Agents, a fully managed harness that makes building your own agent loop feel like unnecessary suffering.

Rounding things out, a developer builds Karpathy’s LLM Wiki idea twice (once as Python, once as a single .md file) to explore where code ends and agent instructions begin. Simon Willison delivers his trademark lightning-speed recap of six months of LLM developments at PyCon US 2026.
